correctness.rationale: Root circular spacings at a specified sampled vertex (not at the first vertex after a fixed coordinate angle); then the uniform simplex density is valid. On the exclusion event the unique long gap is greater than π; disjointness and Dirichlet slicing give probability n/2^(n-1), independent T=δ/π with survival (1-t)^(n-1), and V of dimension m=n-1, uniform on its simplex. The closing chord and its oriented area contribution are 2cos(δ/2) and -sin(δ)/2. For Q=sum V_j³, the Dirichlet moment formula gives mean 6/[(m+1)(m+2)]; its second moment is [720+36(m-1)]/[(m+1)...(m+5)], which yields the frozen variance. With G_j=L V_j, the remainder in the cubic expansions is bounded by a constant times sum G_j⁵, with expectation O(n^-4) uniformly in L. Thus ΔP=δ+δ²/4+L³Q/24 up to O(δ⁴) and the fifth-power error; ΔA=δ+L³Q/12 up to O(δ³) and the fifth-power error. This verifies the shared exponential leading term and the quadratic difference. For W unit-exponential, the delta-method influence for the cube sum normalized by the cubed sample mean is W³-18W+12 of variance 360, giving variance 360π⁶/24²=5π⁶/8. Its normalized spacing vector is exactly independent of the endpoint gap and L tends to π, which proves the joint independence in the limit. The centering in the formula is the exact conditional mean of the cubic proxy, not of the nonlinear D_n; Scope states this correctly and the nonlinear conditional mean differs uniformly by O(n^-4). I inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py without running the frozen script. The finite arithmetic and simulation are diagnostic, not a proof or historical attestation.
